sense: twice as much; made of two

terms.gloss: double, twofold: made of two, or having two parts
evidence: Phaedr. 1 prol. 3: duplex libellī dōs est
Caes. B.G. 2.29.3: duplicī altissimō mūrō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a thing made of two or with two parts: a double wall, a double gift. Of character it means two-faced, deceitful: duplex Ulixēs (Hor. C. 1.6.7, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: twice as much, twice as large
terms.grammar: adjective; as a noun, duplum, duplī n., the double
evidence: Cato Agr. praef. 1: fūrem duplī condemnārī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of amounts and prices: duplum, twice the sum; in duplum, twofold; duplō major, twice as big (Plin.). Duplex says what a thing is made of, duplus how much there is.

terms.gloss: as much again, twice as much
terms.grammar: phrase: alter and the neuter of tantus
evidence: Plaut. Epid. 518–519: etiam sī alterum tantum perdundumst
Cic. Or. 188: partem pedis aut aequālem esse alterī partī aut alterō tantō aut sēsqui esse majōrem, one part of a foot equal to the other, or twice as long, or half as long again
terms.comment: Where English doubles, Latin often counts “the same amount a second time”.

phrases.latin: duplex libellī dōs est: quod rīsum movet et quod prūdentī vītam cōnsiliō monet
phrases.english: the little book’s gift is double: it makes you laugh, and it guides your life with wise advice

phrases.latin: ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est. ejus duplex virtūs, facile percipere et fidēliter continēre
phrases.english: in little ones the chief sign of talent is memory; and its strength is double: to take things in easily and to keep them faithfully

phrases.latin: immō etiam sī alterum tantum perdundumst, perdam potius quam sinam mē impūne irrīsum esse
phrases.english: no: even if I have to lose as much again, I’d rather lose it than let them laugh at me and get away with it
